chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from al-Husayn ibn Ubaydullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Musa ibn Umar, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him). He said:

I asked him about the words of God, Blessed and Exalted: 'They intend to extinguish the light of God with their mouths' [61:8]. He said: 'They intend to extinguish the wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) with their mouths.'
I said: His words, the Exalted: 'but God will complete His light.' He said: 'He means: And God will complete the Imamate; and the Imamate — it is the Light.'
And this is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: 'Believe in God and His Messenger and the Light which We have sent down' [64:8].
He said: 'The Light — it is the Imam.'

key_terms.الإمامة: Imamate — the institution of divinely-guided leadership after the Prophet
key_terms.نور الله: The Light of God — interpreted here as the wilayah of Ali and the Imamate
key_terms.وَلَايَةَ: Wilayah — divine guardianship, authority, the bond of allegiance to the Imam

ai.seo_question: What does 'the Light of Allah' mean in Shia interpretation of Quran 61:8?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a Shia esoteric interpretation of two Quranic verses (61:8 and 64:8) by Abu al-Hasan (likely Imam al-Ridha). The Imam explains that 'the Light of Allah' mentioned in the Quran refers specifically to the wilayah (divine guardianship) of Imam Ali and more broadly to the institution of the Imamate itself, establishing a direct equivalence: Light = Imamate = the Imam. This interpretation would have resonated profoundly with the early Shia community who understood the Imamate as the divinely-ordained continuation of prophetic guidance after the Prophet Muhammad.
